newsitem.title: USA: US meat export group targets Korean hypermarts.
newsitem.headline: US meat export group targets Korean hypermarts.

text.p: The U.S. Meat Export Federation said it will change its strategy for South Korea in 1997 to target beef sales to hypermarts.

"In the early stages of liberalization we focused our resources primarily on importers and the foodservice sector to establish a beachhead for U.S. beef," said USMEF president and CEO Philip Seng in a statement issued here at the National Cattlemen's Beef Association annual convention.
"Now, with more access to end users, we plan to step up our activity in the retail sector to help open doors for U.S. suppliers," he said.
USMEF estimates that 80 percent of U.S. beef sales to Korea are currently going to Korean hotels and restaurants with only 20 percent going to the retail sector.

Hypermarts in Korea are large stores that sell food and other items at discount prices, usually in bulk quantities. While the Korean retail sector in 1997 is expected to be weaker than in recent years, industry experts say the number of hypermarts and their share of retail sales will grow, USMEF said.
The number has already grown to around 100, from none just two years ago, it said.

Korea is expanding its import quotas for beef each year under the Uruguay Round Agreement of the General Agreement on Tarriffs and Trade. Full liberalization of the Korean beef market is scheduled for 2001.
USMEF's goal for 1997 sales to Korea is 100,000 tonnes, up 25 percent from 1996 levels. Korea is the third largest market for U.S. beef, behind only Japan and Canada.
